- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5 days); apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 5 forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model may misread trend direction; favor smoother, trend-following adjustments over abrupt reversals.
